## Design

### 2026-10-22 – This week deciding what to make as a not particularly musically inclined individual was the first hurdle I had to cross. Wanting to somewhat prepare for future projects and learn a new skill regardles

**5h**

This week deciding what to make as a not particularly musically inclined individual was the first hurdle I had to cross. Wanting to somewhat prepare for future projects and learn a new skill regardless of what comes out I decides to go fully analog with a audio amplifier! I knew there are some very high end  amps out there (that also look the price)

![stereoamplifiers-2048px-lede-5-2x1-1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/3002c15d5d4e09aca1390c891ca6a82516527739172b3aaa570af15d63a1ce5a.webp)

By looking through many of these I decided what my requirements and goal for this project should be. I decided that it should be a basic amplifier (volume) with a high and low pass filter (so treble and bass) , and both mono and stereo output. For most of this functionality I chose the  TI NE5532 .

![Screenshot 2026-10-22 at 09.39.54](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/7f75a1ebc89e8ef63203abbe92a962081bb4594102e485897c356cf4e447d8cd.png)

Since I also wanted a very pretty looking design I wanted analog indicators sort of along the lines of

![Screenshot 2026-10-22 at 09.23.34](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/35229133093fd8bca52a25c33f6ef27fcc0e200707b9b6e3d9e1eee0f9fba895.png)

TI used to have a nice analog driver for such applications the LM3914.

![Screenshot 2026-10-22 at 09.39.38](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/7d138e4d86dda1c3bd9b61ed6472592b472803ec84f589affb4bb68a4c1d9e94.png)

However it seems to have been discontinued by them a while ago. Lucky me. the Chinese have everything I could need and the datasheet of the XBLW LM 3915 looks practically identical (the diagrams are the same and the rest I can't read...) the only difference is that it has a internal logarithmic divider so it's almost better suited for this application.

Then I half started doing a schematic in Fusion until I realized that given that I want to simulate it all it might be smarter to us KICad - tiny learning curve later and a few imported components and a lot of looking at other examples and understanding the inner workings later I ended up with my first schematic.
![KICAD Analog Audio Amp](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/4cd69c72664521b658685edf868b00ec7af7452bf5b46e7fd4213807c46b8dcf.webp)

Next time I have time I will read into how to simulate my schematic and do that and maybe work on a CAD enclosure inbetween.
